tables.name: depth_model_benchmarks
tables.units: params in millions; latency ms per image; DA-2K accuracy %; delta1 and AbsRel unitless
rows: Depth Anything V2 (ablation: labelled synthetic only)
Depth Anything V2 (ablation: pseudo-labelled real only)
tables.population: General indoor/outdoor scene benchmarks (DA-2K, NYU-D, SUN-RGBD); no face data. Latency hardware not stated.
tables.notes: Values from search-result summaries of the papers. The alphaXiv URL mirrors arXiv, so it is not independent. That DA V2 relative checkpoints output disparity, and that the ViT-L NYU-D row is the in-domain metric fine-tuned setting, are expert knowledge (unverified). DA3Metric-Large param count is from a community wrapper. DA3-metric is also reported 2nd best on DIODE (value not retrieved).

tables.name: normal_model_benchmarks
tables.units: mean angular error in degrees; training image count
tables.population: NYUv2 indoor scenes; no face data
tables.notes: 'verified' applies only to the 16.4 deg NYUv2 error, which two independent later papers cite. The training image counts (~160K vs >12M) come from one source with unclear attribution, so they are 'sourced'. The Omnidata-V2 figure is a lower bound ('over 12M').

tables.name: sapiens_human_depth_normal
tables.population: Full-body human datasets (Hi4D, THuman2); face region not reported
tables.notes: Baselines for the relative improvements were not verified. A claimed 500K-image synthetic fine-tuning set was excluded because its attribution was unclear. Model sizes (0.3B-2B) and the 1024x768 input are expert knowledge, so they are kept in model_runtime_licence_inventory.

tables.name: da3_metric_conversion
tables.units: focal in pixels; output in model metric unit (likely metres, unverified)
tables.notes: Depth is linear in the supplied focal: a fractional focal error gives the same fractional error in distance and relief. Verified 2026-11-20: the official README states the output is metric depth in metres. Not confirmed: whether focal_px refers to the original image or the network processing resolution. Sanity-check against the PnP-solved camera translation.

tables.name: model_runtime_licence_inventory
tables.units: params; input px; CPU seconds per image (order-of-magnitude estimate)
tables.population: Model families as distributed; CPU = typical desktop CPU, single image
tables.notes: Expert knowledge, not checked against sources. CPU timings are rough order-of-magnitude estimates, not measurements. Verify every licence before bundling or recommending weights. Verified 2026-11-20 against the official Depth-Anything-V2 README: Small is Apache-2.0; Base/Large/Giant are CC-BY-NC-4.0. Sapiens licence not confirmed (official README points to a LICENSE file; a third-party wrapper says CC BY-NC 4.0). The source URLs support only the DA3 TensorRT path and the DA3Metric-Large size.

tables.name: disparity_vs_depth_fit_error_and_ray_obliquity
tables.population: Derived numerically: least-squares affine fit of depth z against 1/z over a 100 mm depth interval starting at the camera distance; ray angle = atan(70/z)
tables.notes: Pure derivation; 100 mm visible facial relief is an assumption. Error is bowl-shaped (biases profile). Approximation: max error ~ D^2/(8z) to D^2/(4z). Ray obliquity is the normal-direction error from orthographic integration of a feature 70 mm off-axis.

tables.name: face_pixel_footprint
tables.population: Adult face, bizygomatic width assumed 130-140 mm
tables.notes: Derived arithmetic. Pores (~0.05-0.25 mm) are unresolvable at all listed settings.

tables.name: vmf_kappa_from_mean_angular_error
tables.population: von Mises-Fisher on S2, high-concentration approximation kappa = pi/(2 m^2), m in radians
tables.notes: Derived; a Monte-Carlo check at kappa=19.2 gave mean 16.5 deg, median 15.5 deg. Real predictor errors are heavy-tailed, so use with a robust loss.

tables.name: suggested_engine_defaults
tables.population: Fitting-engine starting points for adult faces photographed at 0.3-1.5 m
tables.notes: Unsourced expert suggestions; tune on synthetic renders and scanned heads before relying on them.
